measurement: where the cost of one rung-2 verification goes
why: The life-inspired-algorithm round's one surviving efficiency claim reduced to caching a deterministic verifier, and its pre-registered kill condition was: if importing a precompiled spec beats inlining it by more than the host noise floor, the remaining win is a build-system fix with no evolutionary layer and no biology. verify_against_spec inlines the frozen spec body into every audit file, so every call re-elaborates the spec.
host_note: Timings are wall-clock `lake env lean` on a warm host, n=5 each. They are NOT a characterised distribution; the point of reporting the spread is that it bounds what any efficiency claim here can resolve.

noise_floor.reading: Identical input varies by up to this factor, so an efficiency claim below it is unmeasurable on this host. The round's own threshold was 1.65x.

findings: The frozen spec dominates: its median elaboration is 12.6s of the audit file's 16.5s, so the candidate and its obligation add a minority of the cost.

Same-input spread reaches 1.88x (spec) and 1.53x (audit). A 1.65x efficiency threshold sits close to that, so the round was right that no pre-registration is legitimate until resolution is characterised with many more repeats.

Because the spec is re-elaborated per call, importing it as a precompiled module is a build-system change available with no evolutionary layer -- which is exactly the pre-registered condition under which the remaining claim must re-justify itself or be dropped.
not_established: n=5 is too small to characterise the distribution; the recommended k=20 was not run.
The spec-as-import path was NOT built or measured, so the size of that saving is unknown -- only that the cost it would remove is the majority of a call.
Nothing here measures any evolutionary or biological mechanism.
